body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honors `include_<attr>?` (with the question mark); this file uses that form everywhere else, e.g. `include_email?`. `include_website_name` is never called, so the conditional does nothing and `website_name` is serialized for every user, as `null` when there's no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

The 'same parent domain' check is wrong. It drops only the first label and compares what's left, so it treats any two hosts with the same number of labels under a shared public suffix as the same site. Examples: `foo.co.uk` vs `forum.co.uk`, and `attacker.github.io` vs `forum.github.io`. In those cases an unrelated external site gets its full path shown as if it belonged to this instance, which undermines the goal of only expanding URLs on our own domain. It also misses legitimate cases where the label counts differ (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `example.com` goes through the else branch and shows only the host). Use a real registrable-domain comparison, or limit this to exact-host / subdomain-of-website matches.

The host comparisons are case-sensitive and ignore a trailing dot. `URI#host` keeps the case from the input, so a website such as `http://Example.com/user` won't match `example.com`. Downcase both hosts before comparing. Also, when there's no scheme (e.g. `example.com/user`), `URI(...).host` is nil, so `website_name` is nil and the template now hides the website completely. That's the same as the old JS split behavior, but it's worth handling while this code is being rewritten.

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal. That breaks under `# frozen_string_literal: true` (FrozenError). Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. Separately, `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times in this method, and `discourse_host.split('.')` is computed repeatedly. Parse once and reuse the result.
